papers.abstract: BackgroundImproved understanding of how variants cause breakthrough infection, despite pre-existing immunity, is needed to advance development of next-generation SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, including those that may provide cross-variant protection or block transmission. SARS-CoV-2 controlled human infection models (CHIMs) may therefore identify correlates of protection and accelerate the development of new interventions. MethodsHealthy vaccinated adults aged 18-30 years were inoculated intranasally in a stepwise dose- escalation CHIM with doses from 1x102 TCID50 to 1x106 TCID50 of SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. Within the 1x106 TCID50 group, participants were selected for serum neutralising antibody titres (NT50) [≤]1:80. Post-inoculation, participants were quarantined for up to 14 days. Outpatient follow-up continued for 12 months. The primary aim was to elicit safe, well-tolerated Delta SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection at a rate of over 50%. FindingsForty-six participants were inoculated; 22 during dose-escalation with no resultant infections, and 24 at the highest dose, of whom 18 were screened for low serum neutralising antibodies. Sustained infection with mild-to-moderate symptoms occurred in 33% (6/18) of the sero- selected group, with highly variable viral loads, viral emissions and symptoms. Serum neutralising antibody, anti-N IgG and to a lesser extent, mucosal anti-S IgA and N-specific T cells most strongly predicted protection from virologically-defined infection. Higher neutralisation, serum and nasal anti-N IgG level, and N-specific T cell responses correlated with lower viral load, while baseline nasal anti-S IgA was associated with lower symptom scores. Transient infection was additionally observed in 6 participants and was associated with higher baseline N-specific T cell responses than those that developed sustained infection. InterpretationSusceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection in those with hybrid immunity is strongly associated with low levels of pre-existing antibody, but the diversity of immune markers associated with protection implies that additional benefits may be conferred by multi-pronged immunity. FundingWellcome Trust Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSTo identify other published SARS-CoV-2 controlled human infection models (CHIM), a search on PubMed was carried out on 4th March 2026. The search terms used were (("controlled human infection") OR ("human challenge")) and ((SARS-CoV-2) OR (COVID-19)) and ("clinical trial"). Two clinical studies were identified. The first study involved healthy adult 18-29 year olds, seronegative to SARS-CoV-2 inoculated with 1x101 TCID50 pre-Alpha (wild-type) SARS-CoV-2. Eighteen of 34 (53%) participants became infected. The model was safe and well-tolerated and there were no study-related serious adverse events. Mild to moderate symptoms were reported by 16 of 18 (89%) infected individuals while 2 had virtually no symptoms. 14 of 18 (78%) of participants reported smell disturbance measured by the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT). Viral detection by qPCR became quantifiable in throat swabs from 40 hours ([~]1.67 days) post- inoculation and nose swabs at 58 hours ([~]2.4 days). Viral load peaked in the throat at 112 hours ([~]4.2 days) post-inoculation and later at 148 hours ([~]6.2 days) post-inoculation in the nose. The second study involved healthy adult 18-30 year olds, seropositive to SARS-CoV-2 inoculated with escalating doses (1x101-1x105 TCID50) of the same pre-Alpha variant. Thirty- six participants were inoculated and no sustained infection meeting the protocol-defined definition of infection was induced. Five (14%) of 36 volunteers were considered to have transient (brief) infections, based on the kinetic of their PCR-positive swabs. In the first study, functionally-complete protection was associated with early increases in innate and adaptive cell abundance in the nose post-inoculation, higher pre-existing chemokine levels (particularly CCL13) in the nasal lining fluid and cross-reactive T cell responses. Transient infections (PCR positivity outside of residual inoculum not meeting the protocol- defined criteria for infection) were present in both studies. In the second study, transient infection was associated with significantly lower baseline mucosal and systemic SARS-CoV- 2 antibody levels and significantly lower peripheral IFN-{gamma} producing CD8+ T-cell against a SARS-CoV-2 peptide pool than uninfected participants. Added value of this studyWith near-universal seropositivity to SARS-CoV-2, understanding the factors that influence how variants cause breakthrough infection is critical. The optimisation of a model that can induce safe and tolerable infection in a large proportion of participants is necessary for SARS- CoV-2 CHIMs to be used as a tool for next-generation vaccine development. Our study is the first SARS-CoV-2 CHIM of seropositive individuals to induce sustained, protocol defined infection, albeit with an infection rate of 33%. Despite the low number of infected individuals, we identified several potential correlates of protection against breakthrough Delta SARS-CoV-2 infection beyond serum neutralising antibodies. Implications of all the available evidenceThis study establishes the framework for SARS-CoV-2 CHIM conduct, using sero-selection to increase attack rate in the same way it is used for influenza human challenge studies, and a process for defining quantitative correlates of protection. Further work will optimise model parameters with Omicron subvariants to result in infection rates of [≥]50% to support testing of novel interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated biomarkers of protection against SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant breakthrough infection using a controlled human infection model (CHIM) in healthy vaccinated adults aged 18-30 years. Participants were inoculated intranasally with escalating doses of Delta variant, with sero-selection for low neutralising antibody titres. The primary aim was to achieve a breakthrough infection rate of over 50%. Results showed that 33% of the sero-selected group developed sustained infection, with serum neutralising antibody, anti-N IgG, mucosal anti-S IgA, and N-specific T cells strongly predicting protection. Higher neutralisation and antibody levels correlated with lower viral load, while baseline nasal anti-S IgA was associated with lower symptom scores. The study establishes a framework for SARS-CoV-2 CHIM conduct and identifies multi-pronged immunity as beneficial for protection against breakthrough infection.

elements_en.main_results: Sustained infection with mild-to-moderate symptoms occurred in 33% (6/18) of the sero-selected group; serum neutralising antibody, anti-N IgG, mucosal anti-S IgA, and N-specific T cells most strongly predicted protection from virologically-defined infection, with higher neutralisation and antibody levels correlating with lower viral load.

papers.title_zh: 预防受控人类 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Delta 变异突破性感染的生物标志物
papers.source_body_en: BackgroundImproved understanding of how variants cause breakthrough infection, despite pre-existing immunity, is needed to advance development of next-generation SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, including those that may provide cross-variant protection or block transmission. SARS-CoV-2 controlled human infection models (CHIMs) may therefore identify correlates of protection and accelerate the development of new interventions. MethodsHealthy vaccinated adults aged 18-30 years were inoculated intranasally in a stepwise dose- escalation CHIM with doses from 1x102 TCID50 to 1x106 TCID50 of SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. Within the 1x106 TCID50 group, participants were selected for serum neutralising antibody titres (NT50) [≤]1:80. Post-inoculation, participants were quarantined for up to 14 days. Outpatient follow-up continued for 12 months. The primary aim was to elicit safe, well-tolerated Delta SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection at a rate of over 50%. FindingsForty-six participants were inoculated; 22 during dose-escalation with no resultant infections, and 24 at the highest dose, of whom 18 were screened for low serum neutralising antibodies. Sustained infection with mild-to-moderate symptoms occurred in 33% (6/18) of the sero- selected group, with highly variable viral loads, viral emissions and symptoms. Serum neutralising antibody, anti-N IgG and to a lesser extent, mucosal anti-S IgA and N-specific T cells most strongly predicted protection from virologically-defined infection. Higher neutralisation, serum and nasal anti-N IgG level, and N-specific T cell responses correlated with lower viral load, while baseline nasal anti-S IgA was associated with lower symptom scores. Transient infection was additionally observed in 6 participants and was associated with higher baseline N-specific T cell responses than those that developed sustained infection. InterpretationSusceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infection in those with hybrid immunity is strongly associated with low levels of pre-existing antibody, but the diversity of immune markers associated with protection implies that additional benefits may be conferred by multi-pronged immunity. FundingWellcome Trust Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSTo identify other published SARS-CoV-2 controlled human infection models (CHIM), a search on PubMed was carried out on 4th March 2026. The search terms used were (("controlled human infection") OR ("human challenge")) and ((SARS-CoV-2) OR (COVID-19)) and ("clinical trial"). Two clinical studies were identified. The first study involved healthy adult 18-29 year olds, seronegative to SARS-CoV-2 inoculated with 1x101 TCID50 pre-Alpha (wild-type) SARS-CoV-2. Eighteen of 34 (53%) participants became infected. The model was safe and well-tolerated and there were no study-related serious adverse events. Mild to moderate symptoms were reported by 16 of 18 (89%) infected individuals while 2 had virtually no symptoms. 14 of 18 (78%) of participants reported smell disturbance measured by the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT). Viral detection by qPCR became quantifiable in throat swabs from 40 hours ([~]1.67 days) post- inoculation and nose swabs at 58 hours ([~]2.4 days). Viral load peaked in the throat at 112 hours ([~]4.2 days) post-inoculation and later at 148 hours ([~]6.2 days) post-inoculation in the nose. The second study involved healthy adult 18-30 year olds, seropositive to SARS-CoV-2 inoculated with escalating doses (1x101-1x105 TCID50) of the same pre-Alpha variant. Thirty- six participants were inoculated and no sustained infection meeting the protocol-defined definition of infection was induced. Five (14%) of 36 volunteers were considered to have transient (brief) infections, based on the kinetic of their PCR-positive swabs. In the first study, functionally-complete protection was associated with early increases in innate and adaptive cell abundance in the nose post-inoculation, higher pre-existing chemokine levels (particularly CCL13) in the nasal lining fluid and cross-reactive T cell responses. Transient infections (PCR positivity outside of residual inoculum not meeting the protocol- defined criteria for infection) were present in both studies. In the second study, transient infection was associated with significantly lower baseline mucosal and systemic SARS-CoV- 2 antibody levels and significantly lower peripheral IFN-{gamma} producing CD8+ T-cell against a SARS-CoV-2 peptide pool than uninfected participants. Added value of this studyWith near-universal seropositivity to SARS-CoV-2, understanding the factors that influence how variants cause breakthrough infection is critical. The optimisation of a model that can induce safe and tolerable infection in a large proportion of participants is necessary for SARS- CoV-2 CHIMs to be used as a tool for next-generation vaccine development. Our study is the first SARS-CoV-2 CHIM of seropositive individuals to induce sustained, protocol defined infection, albeit with an infection rate of 33%. Despite the low number of infected individuals, we identified several potential correlates of protection against breakthrough Delta SARS-CoV-2 infection beyond serum neutralising antibodies. Implications of all the available evidenceThis study establishes the framework for SARS-CoV-2 CHIM conduct, using sero-selection to increase attack rate in the same way it is used for influenza human challenge studies, and a process for defining quantitative correlates of protection. Further work will optimise model parameters with Omicron subvariants to result in infection rates of [≥]50% to support testing of novel interventions.

papers.title: Modeling the public health impact of vaccination with Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, LP.8.1, 2025–2026 formula in the pediatric population aged 5–17 years at high risk of severe outcomes from COVID-19 in the United States
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study evaluated the potential public health impact of receiving Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, LP.8.1, 2025-2026 formula, in the US pediatric population aged 5-17 years at high risk of severe outcomes from COVID-19. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A previously published static decision-tree model was adapted to compare health outcomes with and without vaccination. Demographic, epidemiological, vaccine (effectiveness, vaccine uptake), and clinical model inputs were derived from surveillance data and relevant published studies. RESULTS: In the absence of LP.8.1-adapted BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccination, COVID-19 burden among those aged 5-11 years and 12-17 years was projected as 1,007,114 and 1,467,724 symptomatic cases, 2,493 and 2,547 hospitalizations, and 109 and 107 COVID-19-related deaths, respectively. Assuming observed 2024-2025 uptake levels of 8.7% and 8.6% among those aged 5-11 and 12-17 years, respectively, LP.8.1-adapted BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccination was projected to avert 4,387 and 7,146 symptomatic cases, 27 and 31 hospitalizations, and 1 death in each age group, respectively. Increasing uptake to 50% would increase the health burden averted 6-fold. CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of an LP.8.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccine was projected to reduce the COVID-19 burden in the high-risk pediatric population, even with low vaccine uptake. Increasing vaccine uptake in this population could yield larger public health impact.

analysis.summary_en: This study assesses the potential public health impact of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, LP.8.1, 2025-2026 formula, in the US pediatric population aged 5-17 years at high risk of severe outcomes from COVID-19. A static decision-tree model was adapted to compare health outcomes with and without vaccination. The model inputs were derived from surveillance data and published studies. The results project that without vaccination, the burden of symptomatic cases, hospitalizations, and deaths would be substantial, but vaccination could avert these cases even with low uptake. Increasing vaccine uptake is projected to yield larger public health benefits. The study's reliance on a static model and assumed uptake levels may limit the confidence in its projections. The findings suggest that vaccination could significantly reduce the burden of severe outcomes in high-risk pediatric populations, emphasizing the importance of increasing vaccine coverage.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches
papers.abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic highlighted the critical need for rapid, accessible, and accurate diagnostic tools to support timely clinical decision-making, outbreak control, and public health surveillance. Point-of-care testing (POCT) has emerged as an essential component of decentralized healthcare by enabling diagnostic testing outside conventional laboratory settings. This review was based on a structured literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases covering studies published between January 2020 and January 2026. The review evaluates current advances in COVID-19 POCT technologies, including molecular assays, antigen-based tests, antibody-based assays, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular POCT methods, including rapid reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and CRISPR-based technologies, provide high analytical sensitivity and specificity and are increasingly suitable for decentralized diagnostic applications. Antigen-based assays offer rapid and cost-effective screening solutions, although diagnostic performance may vary depending on viral load, symptom onset, and circulating variants. Antibody-based POCT remains valuable for seroprevalence studies, retrospective diagnosis, and immune-response monitoring rather than acute infection detection. Emerging biosensor technologies and AI-enabled diagnostic systems demonstrate promising analytical capabilities and operational advantages; however, many remain at the prototype or early-validation stage and require further clinical evaluation before widespread implementation. The findings indicate that no single POCT modality is optimal for all clinical scenarios. Instead, molecular, antigen, antibody, biosensor, and AI-assisted approaches provide complementary strengths that support different diagnostic and public health objectives. Continued advances in assay design, digital connectivity, multiplex testing, and variant-resilient detection strategies are expected to further enhance the role of POCT in COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.

papers.title: Effects of COVID-19 Control Policies on Malaria Surveillance: A Comparative Analysis of North and South Korea.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Both South and North Korea are identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having the potential to eliminate malaria. However, the increase in malaria cases during the COVID-19 response has prompted an investigation into the reasons behind this unexpected rise. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Epidemiological, entomological, and meteorological data from national and international surveillance systems were analyzed. Using the WHO's analytical framework, which can be effectively applied during the elimination phase, we assessed drivers of malaria resurgence in North and South Korea. RESULTS: In North Korea, border closures caused a severe shortage of rapid diagnostic test kits, reducing malaria testing by over 90% by 2021. Microscopy use increased but remained insufficient, while confirmed cases rose from 1819 in 2020 to 3160 in 2023. In South Korea, public health resources were diverted to COVID-19, weakening malaria control activities. The response time for epidemiological investigations increased from 1.3 days in 2019 to 4.3 days in 2021. Relapse cases, which were zero in 2021, increased to eight in 2023, and confirmed cases rose from 274 in 2021 to 673 in 2023. There were no meaningful changes in the drivers of malaria resurgence, including importation of malaria parasites or human susceptibility. With no notable shifts in vector density, variations in temperature and precipitation did not explain the rise in either country, and there were no reports of emerging resistance to insecticides or antimalarial drugs. CONCLUSION: These COVID-19-related disruptions, including supply chain failures and the diversion of human resources, impaired malaria control in countries on the Korean Peninsula.

papers.title: Low reporting quality limits the contribution of human organ models to COVID-19 research: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic created a unique situation in which researchers repurposed human models of varying complexity to investigate SARS-CoV-2, providing the opportunity to analyse their contribution across organs. Methods We conducted a systematic review of 558 studies, divided into pandemic and post-pandemic periods, to assess how human models were applied to investigate host factors, viral replication of SARS-CoV-2, immune responses, and to evaluate reporting quality. Findings Our analysis revealed substantial limitations that were only partially alleviated in post-pandemic studies. These limitations included heterogeneity of outcome measures, incomplete documentation of model characteristics and experimental procedures, and variable reporting quality, which were associated with reduced cross-study comparability, more difficult risk-of-bias assessment, and limited reliability and interpretability of evidence synthesis and meta-analytical results. Interpretation Strengthening community-driven reporting standards and methodological transparency is essential to enable robust evidence synthesis and to fully realise the potential of human organ models in future pandemics and translational research. Funding The study was supported by Einstein Foundation Berlin; Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space; European Union; Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung; Volkswagen Foundation; Charité 3R; Foundation Charité.

papers.title: Long-term Cardiovascular Outcomes in US Medicare Beneficiaries After COVID-19 Hospitalization During the Omicron Era.
papers.abstract: Background COVID-19 hospitalization in the pre-Omicron era was associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, but data from the Omicron era are sparse. We examined the risk of death and major adverse cardiovascular events among older adults hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron era compared with the pre-Omicron era and a historical influenza cohort. Methods Retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥65 years hospitalized for COVID-19 in the Omicron era (November 2021-September2022), COVID-19 in the pre-Omicron era (March 2020-November 2021), and influenza (October 2017-September 2018). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and hospitalization for myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, heart failure, and cardiac arrest within 1 year of the index admission. We standardized the cohorts using inverse probability weighting. Results We included 1 184 182 patients (mean age 79 years; 51% women):361 382 in the Omicron cohort, 731 455 in the pre-Omicron cohort, and 91 345 in the influenza cohort. The risk of the primary outcome in the Omicron cohort was lower than in the pre-Omicron cohort (48.8% versus 49.3%; standardized risk difference, -0.6% [95% CI, -0.8% to -0.3%]) but higher than in the influenza cohort (48.8% versus 33.4%; risk difference, 15.4% [15.1%-15.6%]). Compared with the pre-Omicron cohort, the Omicron cohort had a significantly lower risk of death (34.2% versus 39.7%; risk difference, -5.5% [-5.7% to -5.3%]) but a higher risk of myocardial infarction, stroke or transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, and heart failure. Conclusions Among older adults hospitalized with COVID-19, the risk of death within 1 year was lower, and the risk of major adverse cardiovascular event was higher in the Omicron era than the pre-Omicron era; however, the risk of either outcome was higher than after influenza hospitalization. These findings underscore the need for effective cardiovascular prevention strategies after a COVID-19 hospitalization.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding long-term cardiovascular outcomes in older adults hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron era, as prior data from the pre-Omicron era indicated an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥65 years hospitalized for COVID-19 during the Omicron era (November 2021-September 2022), the pre-Omicron era (March 2020-November 2021), and a historical influenza cohort (October 2017-September 2018).
analysis.methods: The study used inverse probability weighting to standardize the cohorts and compared the risk of death and major adverse cardiovascular events between the Omicron and pre-Omicron cohorts, as well as the influenza cohort.
analysis.main_results: The primary outcome, a composite of all-cause death and cardiovascular events, occurred in 48.8% of the Omicron cohort, 49.3% of the pre-Omicron cohort, and 33.4% of the influenza cohort. The Omicron cohort had a significantly lower risk of death (34.2% vs. 39.7%) but a higher risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, and heart failure compared to the pre-Omicron cohort.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the risk of death was lower in the Omicron era than in the pre-Omicron era, but the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events was higher, highlighting a shift in the post-hospitalization outcomes associated with SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that cardiovascular prevention strategies should be prioritized for older adults recovering from Omicron-related COVID-19 hospitalizations, as the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events remains elevated compared to influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and standardized cohort comparison.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated long-term cardiovascular outcomes in older adults hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron era compared to the pre-Omicron era and a historical influenza cohort. It found that while the risk of death was lower in the Omicron era, the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events was higher than in the pre-Omicron era. The results emphasize the need for targeted cardiovascular prevention strategies post-COVID-19 hospitalization, particularly for those affected by the Omicron variant. The study's large sample size and standardized cohort comparison provide strong evidence, though limitations include the retrospective design and potential confounding factors.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that cardiovascular prevention strategies should be prioritized for older adults recovering from Omicron-related COVID-19 hospitalizations, as the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events remains elevated compared to influenza.
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的混杂因素而受到限制,但由于样本量大和标准化的 队列研究 比较,证据充足。

papers.title: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA Residues in Placenta Tissue Following Maternal COVID-19 Infection During Pregnancy.
papers.abstract: PROBLEM: Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 viral persistence was reported in extrapulmonary tissues in patients infected with COVID-19. SARS-CoV-2 can infect placental tissue. However, little is known about SARS-CoV-2 viral persistence in the placenta. METHOD OF STUDY: This is a retrospective and IRB approved study. Placental tissue samples from 40 women infected with COVID-19 at various gestational age were analyzed. SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression was examined by in situ hybridization on placental disk and fetal membrane. S-protein and N-protein expression was determined by immunostaining. SARS-CoV-2 RNA sequencing was also performed in 12 out of the 29 cases in which SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression was detected positive by in situ hybridization. RESULTS: SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression was detected in placental disk, predominantly localized in syncytiotrophoblasts in 29 out of the 40 cases, but not in fetal membrane. Among the 29 positive cases, 4 infected in the first trimester, 7 in the second trimester, and 18 in the third trimester or at term. The longest interval from infection to delivery was 221 days. Among the 21 women who tested positive for COVID-19 at L/D admission, 18 (85.7%) detected SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression in placental tissue. Notably, 11 (57.9%) of 19 cases (negative test at L/D admission) detected viral RNA expression in placental villous tissue. Viral RNA expression was also detected in villous core vessel endothelium in two COVID (+) newborn placentas, with corresponding positive S-protein and N-protein expression in syncytiotrophoblasts. S-protein and N-protein expression was undetectable in 27 out of the 29 cases with positive detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression. Partial RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) region sequence was identified in all the 12 cases examined. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide compelling evidence that SARS-CoV-2 genetic material can persist in placental tissue long after maternal infection, which may potentially contribute to a sustained inflammatory environment at the maternal-fetal interface during pregnancy. The phenomenon of partial RdRp sequence detected would provide a possible explanation for undetectable S- and N-protein expression in testing specimens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 viral persistence was reported in extrapulmonary tissues in patients infected with COVID-19, but little is known about SARS-CoV-2 viral persistence in the placenta.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a retrospective and IRB approved study analyzing placental tissue samples from 40 women infected with COVID-19 at various gestational age.
analysis.methods: SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression was examined by in situ hybridization on placental disk and fetal membrane, S-protein and N-protein expression was determined by immunostaining, and SARS-CoV-2 RNA sequencing was performed in 12 out of the 29 cases with positive RNA detection.
analysis.main_results: SARS-CoV-2 RNA expression was detected in placental disk, predominantly localized in syncytiotrophoblasts in 29 out of the 40 cases, with the longest interval from infection to delivery being 221 days; viral RNA expression was also detected in villous core vessel endothelium in two COVID (+) newborn placentas.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings provide compelling evidence that SARS-CoV-2 genetic material can persist in placental tissue long after maternal infection, potentially contributing to a sustained inflammatory environment at the maternal-fetal interface during pregnancy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in placental tissue may have implications for understanding the long-term effects of COVID-19 on pregnancy outcomes and fetal development, warranting further investigation into potential clinical monitoring strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the absence of S-protein and N-protein expression in most cases, though the detection of partial RdRp sequence provides a possible explanation for undetectable protein expression; the evidence strength is moderate due to the sample size and methodological constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study investigated SARS-CoV-2 viral persistence in placental tissue from 40 women infected with COVID-19 at various gestational ages. Using in situ hybridization, immunostaining, and RNA sequencing, the researchers detected SARS-CoV-2 RNA in 29 out of 40 placental disk samples, predominantly in syncytiotrophoblasts, with the longest interval from infection to delivery being 221 days. Notably, 57.9% of cases with negative COVID-19 tests at delivery still showed viral RNA expression. While S-protein and N-protein expression was undetectable in most cases, partial RdRp sequences were identified, suggesting viral persistence without active protein production. The findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 genetic material can persist in placental tissue long after maternal infection, potentially contributing to sustained inflammation at the maternal-fetal interface.

papers.abstract_zh: 问题:据报道,在感染 新型冠状病毒感染 的患者的肺外组织中,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 病毒持续存在时间较长。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 可感染胎盘组织。然而,人们对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 病毒在胎盘中的持续存在知之甚少。研究方法:这是一项经 IRB 批准的回顾性研究。对 40 名不同孕龄感染 新型冠状病毒感染 的女性的胎盘组织样本进行了分析。通过原位杂交在胎盘和胎膜上检查严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA 表达。通过免疫染色测定S-蛋白和N-蛋白表达。通过原位杂交检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA表达阳性的29例中的12例也进行了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA测序。结果:40例中的29例在胎盘中检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA表达,主要定位于合体滋养层,但胎膜中未检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA表达。29例阳性病例中,孕早期感染者4例,孕中期感染者7例,孕晚期或足月感染者18例。从感染到分娩的最长间隔为221天。在 L/D 入院时 新型冠状病毒感染 检测呈阳性的 21 名女性中,18 名 (85.7%) 在胎盘组织中检测到 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA 表达。值得注意的是,19 例(L/D 入院时检测呈阴性)中有 11 例(57.9%)在胎盘绒毛组织中检测到病毒 RNA 表达。在两个 COVID(+)新生儿胎盘的绒毛核心血管内皮中也检测到病毒 RNA 表达,在合体滋养层中相应的 S 蛋白和 N 蛋白阳性表达。29例严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA表达阳性的病例中,27例未检测到S蛋白和N蛋白表达。在所有 12 个检查病例中均鉴定出了部分 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 区域序列。结论:这些发现提供了令人信服的证据,表明 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 遗传物质在母体感染后很长时间内可以在胎盘组织中持续存在,这可能有助于怀孕期间母胎界面的持续炎症环境。检测到部分 RdRp 序列的现象将为测试样本中检测不到的 S 和 N 蛋白表达提供可能的解释。

papers.title: Country-level immunization recovery and DTP1 no-dose proxy burden after COVID-19: a descriptive ecological analysis of WUENIC, 2010-2024.
papers.abstract: Background Global immunization averages can obscure entity-level shortfalls in access, series completion, measles coverage, and recovery from 2019. We assessed these signals. Methods The primary analysis used exact-2024-revision WHO/UNICEF WUENIC records for 194 countries/reporting entities during 2010-2024. We estimated recovery from 2019 and DTP1 no-dose proxy burden, quantified DTP3-MCV1 overlap, and assigned ordered phenotypes. We reproduced benchmarks and conducted source-status, target-population-weighted, threshold, and exact-2025-revision sensitivity analyses. Results Reproduced weighted 2024 estimates were 88.94% for DTP1, 84.56% for DTP3, and 84.03% for MCV1. Unweighted country fixed-effects estimates for 2024 versus 2019 were - 1.80 percentage points (95% CI -2.75 to -0.84) for DTP1, -2.09 (-3.25 to -0.93) for DTP3, and - 1.65 (-2.72 to -0.58) for MCV1; target-population-weighted estimates were closer to zero and imprecise. The DTP1 no-dose proxy count was 14.26 million; the top 20 entities accounted for 74.6%. Forty-five entities with DTP3 below 80% and MCV1 below 90% accounted for 72.8% of the proxy count. Threshold changes reassigned at most 13.4% of entities. With exact-2025-revision records and the endpoint fixed at 2024, aggregate metrics were similar, but 20 recovery-class and 19 phenotype assignments changed among 194 common entities. Conclusion Aggregate coverage near 2019 levels coexisted with entity-level access, completion, measles, recovery, and data-review signals. Program managers should review them jointly, not as one ranking; assignments are descriptive and revision-specific, not validated risk scores.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines country-level immunization recovery and DTP1 no-dose proxy burden after COVID-19, focusing on access, series completion, measles coverage, and recovery from 2019 across 194 countries/reporting entities during 2010-2024.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A descriptive ecological analysis using exact-2024-revision WHO/UNICEF WUENIC records, with estimation of recovery, DTP1 no-dose burden, DTP3-MCV1 overlap, and phenotype assignments. Benchmarks were reproduced, and sensitivity analyses included source-status, target-population-weighted, threshold, and exact-2025-revision approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Aggregate immunization coverage in 2024 was near 2019 levels (DTP1: 88.94%, DTP3: 84.56%, MCV1: 84.03%), but country-level fixed-effects estimates showed declines (-1.80 to -2.09 percentage points). The DTP1 no-dose proxy burden was 14.26 million, with the top 20 entities accounting for 74.6%, and 45 entities with low DTP3/Measles coverage representing 72.8% of the burden.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Threshold changes reassigned at most 13.4% of entities, and 2025 data revisions altered 20 recovery-class and 19 phenotype assignments among 194 common entities. Assignments are descriptive and revision-specific, not validated risk scores, and may not fully capture nuanced recovery patterns.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Program managers should jointly review entity-level signals for access, completion, measles coverage, recovery, and data quality rather than relying on single rankings. Descriptive phenotypes require contextual interpretation and should not be used as standalone risk metrics.

analysis.summary_en: This ecological analysis of WHO/UNICEF WUENIC data (2010-2024) reveals that while global immunization coverage rebounded to near-2019 levels by 2024, significant country-level disparities persist. DTP1 no-dose proxy burden reached 14.26 million, concentrated in 45 low-coverage entities. Fixed-effects estimates showed declines in DTP1, DTP3, and MCV1 coverage from 2019 to 2024. Phenotype assignments are descriptive and revision-specific, requiring joint interpretation of multiple signals rather than single rankings. Program managers must prioritize context-specific recovery strategies and avoid over-reliance on aggregate metrics.

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 项目经理应联合审查实体层面的访问、完成、麻疹覆盖率、恢复和数据质量信号,而不是依赖单一排名。描述性表型需要上下文解释,不应用作独立的风险指标。

papers.title: Tunable Immune Imprinting of Memory B Cells to SARS-CoV-2 Variants 2255300
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Immune imprinting, historically termed “original antigenic sin”, biases memory B cell (MBC) recall toward cross-reactive epitopes of ancestral strains, limiting vaccine adaptability to rapidly evolving variants. Whether immune imprinting is a fixed outcome of antigen exposure or can be modulated by host immune factors remains unclear. Chronic inflammatory and immunosuppressive conditions in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients affect antibody-secreting cell formation during MBC recall responses, but whether these host-intrinsic conditions can modulate MBC epitope targeting and immune imprinting in response to an antigenically distant variant remains unknown. Methods We recruited tightly time-matched cohorts of healthy individuals and SLE patients who had received three doses of ancestral inactivated vaccine and subsequently experienced synchronized Omicron BA.5/BF.7 breakthrough infection. We characterized their MBC responses through monoclonal antibody (mAb) epitope mapping, deep mutational scanning (DMS), spectral flow cytometry, and antigen-linked single-cell multi-omics. Results Healthy individuals displayed strong immune imprinting, characterized by robust recall of high-affinity cross-reactive MBCs. In contrast, SLE patients exhibited markedly reduced imprinting, with DMS revealing enhanced recognition of variant-specific neutralizing epitopes. Antigen-linked single-cell profiling showed attenuated MBC recall in SLE, associated with reduced MBC reactivation, diminished BCR signaling, and heightened inflammatory signatures. Concurrently, naïve and IgM MBCs were recruited and matured into variant-specific IgG MBCs, accompanied by a decline in early self- and polyreactivity. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that immune imprinting in MBCs is plastic, and modulation of inflammatory and B cell activation signaling can rebalance recall versus de novo responses to promote variant-adaptable immunity. Funding Source National Natural Science Foundation of China Topic Categories Lymphocyte Differentiation and Peripheral Maintenance (LYM)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Immune imprinting biases memory B cell recall toward ancestral strains, limiting vaccine adaptability to evolving variants, and whether this imprinting can be modulated by host immune factors remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We recruited tightly time-matched cohorts of healthy individuals and SLE patients who had received three doses of ancestral inactivated vaccine and subsequently experienced synchronized Omicron BA.5/BF.7 breakthrough infection.
analysis.methods: We characterized their MBC responses through monoclonal antibody (mAb) epitope mapping, deep mutational scanning (DMS), spectral flow cytometry, and antigen-linked single-cell multi-omics.
analysis.main_results: Healthy individuals displayed strong immune imprinting with robust recall of high-affinity cross-reactive MBCs, while SLE patients exhibited markedly reduced imprinting with enhanced recognition of variant-specific neutralizing epitopes and attenuated MBC recall.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings demonstrate that immune imprinting in MBCs is plastic, and modulation of inflammatory and B cell activation signaling can rebalance recall versus de novo responses to promote variant-adaptable immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights suggest that targeting inflammatory pathways could enhance vaccine responses against evolving variants, potentially informing strategies to improve COVID-19 vaccine adaptability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it is based on abstract-only data without detailed methods or statistical analyses, limiting assessment of generalizability and potential biases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated immune imprinting in memory B cells (MBCs) following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection. Researchers compared healthy individuals and SLE patients, finding that SLE patients exhibited reduced immune imprinting and enhanced recognition of variant-specific epitopes. The results demonstrate that immune imprinting is plastic and can be modulated by host inflammatory factors, offering insights for improving vaccine adaptability against evolving variants.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 免疫印记使记忆 B 细胞记忆偏向祖先菌株,限制了 疫苗 对进化变异的适应性,并且这种印记是否可以通过 宿主 免疫因子调节仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们招募了时间紧密匹配的健康个体和 SLE 患者的 队列研究,他们接受了三剂祖先灭活的 疫苗,随后经历了同步的 Omicron BA.5/BF.7 突破性感染。
elements_zh.methods: 我们通过单克隆抗体 (mAb) 表位作图、深度突变扫描 (DMS)、光谱流式细胞术和抗原相关单细胞多组学来表征他们的 MBC 反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 健康个体表现出强烈的免疫印记,对高亲和力交叉反应性 MBC 具有强大的回忆,而 SLE 患者表现出明显减少的印记,对变体特异性中和表位的识别增强,并且 MBC 回忆减弱。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的研究结果表明,MBC 中的免疫印记是可塑的,炎症和 B 细胞激活信号传导的调节可以重新平衡回忆与从头反应,从而促进变异适应性免疫。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights suggest that targeting inflammatory pathways could enhance vaccine responses against evolving variants, potentially informing strategies to improve COVID-19 vaccine adaptability.
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它基于仅抽象的数据,没有详细的方法或统计分析,限制了对普遍性和潜在偏差的评估。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 免疫印记,历史上被称为“原始抗原原罪”,使记忆 B 细胞 (MBC) 记忆偏向祖先菌株的交叉反应表位,从而限制了 疫苗 对快速进化变体的适应性。免疫印记是抗原暴露的固定结果还是可以通过 宿主 免疫因子调节仍不清楚。系统性红斑狼疮 (SLE) 患者的慢性炎症和免疫抑制状况会影响 MBC 回忆反应期间抗体分泌细胞的形成,但这些 宿主 内在状况是否可以调节 MBC 表位靶向和免疫印记以响应抗原性遥远变异仍不清楚。方法 我们招募了时间紧密匹配的健康个体和 SLE 患者的 队列研究,他们接受了三剂祖先灭活的 疫苗,随后经历了同步的 Omicron BA.5/BF.7 突破性感染。我们通过单克隆抗体 (mAb) 表位作图、深度突变扫描 (DMS)、光谱流式细胞术和抗原相关单细胞多组学来表征他们的 MBC 反应。结果健康个体表现出强烈的免疫印记,其特征是对高亲和力交叉反应性 MBC 的强大回忆。相比之下,SLE 患者的印记明显减少,DMS 显示对变异特异性中和表位的识别增强。抗原相关单细胞分析显示 SLE 中 MBC 回忆减弱,与 MBC 再激活减少、BCR 信号传导减弱和炎症特征增强相关。同时,幼稚和 IgM MBC 被招募并成熟为变体特异性 IgG MBC,同时伴随着早期自身反应性和多反应性的下降。结论 我们的研究结果表明,MBC 中的免疫印记是可塑的,炎症和 B 细胞激活信号传导的调节可以重新平衡回忆与从头反应,从而促进变异适应性免疫。资金来源 国家自然科学基金面上项目 课题类别 淋巴细胞分化与外周维持(LYM)

analysis_zh.main_results: 健康个体表现出强烈的免疫印记,对高亲和力交叉反应性 MBC 具有强大的回忆,而 SLE 患者表现出明显减少的印记,对变体特异性中和表位的识别增强,并且 MBC 回忆减弱。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的研究结果表明,MBC 中的免疫印记是可塑的,炎症和 B 细胞激活信号传导的调节可以重新平衡回忆与从头反应,从而促进变异适应性免疫。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它基于仅抽象的数据,没有详细的方法或统计分析,限制了对普遍性和潜在偏差的评估。

papers.title: Immunogenicity, reactogenicity, and safety of an mRNA-based seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 multicomponent vaccine, mRNA-1083, in adults aged ≥50 years in Japan.
papers.abstract: A multicomponent vaccine targeting seasonal influenza and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) may reduce disease burden by providing simultaneous protection in a single injection. We report findings from Part 1 (Japan) of a phase 3, Asia-Pacific, randomized, observer-blind study evaluating immunogenicity, reactogenicity, and safety of mRNA-based multicomponent vaccine mRNA-1083, combining influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) antigens. Participants aged ≥50 years were randomized (1:1) to receive mRNA-1083 + placebo or Japan-licensed influenza hemagglutinin (HA) vaccine + mRNA-1273. Overall, 2022 participants were randomized, and 2013 received study intervention. At Day 29, mRNA-1083 elicited noninferior immune responses versus active comparators for all evaluated influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2. Among high-risk participants (aged ≥65 years and 60 to <65 years with ≥1 comorbidity), noninferiority of mRNA-1083 was demonstrated for comparator-matched influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2. In the overall study population, mRNA-1083 demonstrated superiority for the comparator-matched influenza strains and for SARS-CoV-2. At Day 181, immune responses remained above baseline and were comparable to or numerically higher than those elicited by active comparators. Most solicited adverse reactions were grade 1 or 2. There were no cases of myocarditis or pericarditis, and no reported serious adverse events or deaths related to study intervention. Overall, mRNA-1083 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, eliciting noninferior and superior immune responses against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the high-risk and overall study population, respectively. Immune responses were maintained through 6 months post-vaccination. These findings support mRNA-1083 as a single-dose approach to seasonal vaccination against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults ≥50 years. ClinicalTrials.govidentifier: NCT06694389 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06694389).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need for simplified seasonal vaccination by evaluating whether a single mRNA-based multicomponent vaccine could provide simultaneous protection against seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults aged ≥50 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase 3, Asia-Pacific, randomized, observer-blind trial (Part 1 in Japan) enrolled adults aged ≥50 years who were randomized 1:1 to receive mRNA-1083 plus placebo or licensed influenza HA vaccine plus mRNA-1273, with 2022 participants randomized and 2013 receiving study intervention.
analysis.methods: Participants received either mRNA-1083 or active comparators; immunogenicity was assessed at Day 29 and Day 181, and safety/reactogenicity were monitored throughout, including solicited adverse reactions and serious adverse events.
analysis.main_results: At Day 29, mRNA-1083 elicited noninferior immune responses versus active comparators for all evaluated influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2, with superiority demonstrated for comparator-matched influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2 in the overall population.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating that mRNA-1083 can provide simultaneous protection against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in a single injection, representing a novel approach to seasonal vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support mRNA-1083 as a potential single-dose seasonal vaccination strategy against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults aged ≥50 years, with immune responses maintained through 6 months post-vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single phase 3 trial in Japan with short-term follow-up; generalizability to other populations and long-term safety requires further study, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 3, randomized, observer-blind trial in Japan evaluated the immunogenicity, reactogenicity, and safety of the mRNA-based multicomponent vaccine mRNA-1083, which combines seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 antigens, in adults aged ≥50 years. At Day 29, mRNA-1083 elicited noninferior immune responses versus active comparators for all evaluated influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2, with superiority observed for comparator-matched influenza strains and SARS-CoV-2 in the overall population. Immune responses remained above baseline and comparable to or numerically higher than active comparators at Day 181. The vaccine demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, with most solicited adverse reactions being grade 1 or 2, no cases of myocarditis or pericarditis, and no related serious adverse events or deaths. These findings support mRNA-1083 as a single-dose approach to seasonal vaccination against influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in adults ≥50 years, though generalizability and long-term safety require further study.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过评估单一基于 mRNA 的多组分 疫苗 是否可以同时为年龄≥50 岁的成年人提供针对季节性流感和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的保护,解决了对简化季节性 疫苗接种 的公共卫生需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项亚太地区随机、观察者盲法 3 期试验(第 1 部分在日本)招募了年龄≥50 岁的成年人,他们以 1:1 的比例随机接受 mRNA-1083 加安慰剂或许可的流感 HA 疫苗 加 mRNA-1273,其中 2022 名参与者随机分配,2013 名参与者接受研究干预。
elements_zh.methods: 参与者接受 mRNA-1083 或活性比较剂;在第29天和第181天评估免疫原性,并在整个过程中监测安全性/反应原性,包括引起的不良反应和严重不良事件。
elements_zh.main_results: 在第 29 天,对于所有评估的流感毒株和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,mRNA-1083 引发的 免疫应答 与活性比较剂相比不劣势,并且在总体人群中证明了比较剂匹配的流感毒株和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的优越性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明 mRNA-1083 可以在单次注射中同时提供针对流感和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的保护,代表了一种针对季节性 疫苗接种 的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持mRNA-1083作为针对年龄≥50岁成人的流感和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的潜在单剂量季节性疫苗接种策略,免疫应答在疫苗接种后维持6个月。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于在日本进行的一项具有短期随访的 3 期试验;对其他人群的普遍性和长期安全性需要进一步研究,需要进行适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Estimating Time-Inhomogeneous Transition Probabilities from District Level Daily COVID-19 Transmission Data in Sierra Leone
papers.abstract: Abstract: Compartmental epidemic models conventionally treat the probability of moving between dis ease states as fixed over time, an assumption that sits uneasily with the reality of a pandemic in which lockdowns, mask mandates, vaccination roll-out, and the arrival of new variants continually reshape transmission. This paper develops a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain framework for the Susceptible–Exposed–Infectious–Removed (SEIR) process, in which each transition probability pab(t) is allowed to vary with calendar time while respecting the struc tural zeros implied by the SEIR compartmental flow. We derive the constrained maximum likelihood estimator of pab(t) under these structural constraints, establish its finite sample efficiency, asymptotic normality, and Wilson score confidence intervals, and construct a like lihood ratio test of the null hypothesis that a compartment’s exit probability is constant over time. We further propose a stochastic machine learning hybrid extension in which the raw, kernel smoothed transition probabilities are regressed on policy and mobility covariates using both a logistic generalized linear model and a random forest, allowing the framework to attribute time-inhomogeneity to observable interventions. The methodology is applied to a compiled daily, district level COVID-19 surveillance panel for Sierra Leone spanning March 2020 to December 2023 (16 districts, 1,401 days). The likelihood ratio test rejects time-homogeneity of the exposed to infectious transition in 15 of 16 districts and of the infectious-to-removed transition in 8 of 16 districts (α = 0.05), and the covariate augmented logistic model achieves an out of sample Brier score roughly 76 times smaller than a time homogeneous pooled baseline, with healthcare capacity and the time trend emerging as the most influential predictors in the random-forest component. These results provide statisti cal evidence that time-inhomogeneous, covariate informed Markov models offer a materially better description of district-level COVID-19 transmission in Sierra Leone than classical time homogeneous compartmental models, with implications for sub-national outbreak monitoring in resource constrained settings

papers.title: Recovery of proofreading-impaired SARS-CoV-2 reveals a mutator phenotype and an ExoN activity threshold for viability.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Coronaviruses (CoVs) replicate unusually large RNA genomes that necessitate proofreading by the 3′-to-5′ exoribonuclease (ExoN) formed by nonstructural proteins 14 (nsp14) and 10 (nsp10). Previous studies suggested that inactivation of the ExoN catalytic site in severe acute respiratory syndrome CoV 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is lethal, leaving unresolved whether the virus can tolerate impaired proofreading activity. Here, we investigated the functional requirement for ExoN in SARS-CoV-2 replication by combining a continuous fluorescence-based biochemical assay with an optimized single-bacmid reverse genetics system. Mutational analysis of residues involved in RNA binding or catalysis revealed graded effects on ExoN activity in vitro . Alanine substitution of Lys9, a residue positioned near the RNA-binding interface, did not reduce ExoN activity, whereas charge reversal at this position (K9E) impaired activity more strongly than alanine substitutions of the catalytic motif I residues D90 and E92 (D90A/E92A). Correspondingly, recombinant SARS-CoV-2 carrying K9A was readily recovered, whereas the D90A/E92A mutant was recovered only after an extended delay, and K9E could not be rescued despite repeated attempts. The D90A/E92A mutant exhibited reduced replication while maintaining the engineered ExoN substitutions during serial passage. Deep sequencing of viral populations revealed a marked increase in genome-wide sequence variation in the D90A/E92A mutant, demonstrating a stable mutator phenotype. Together, these findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate substantial impairment of ExoN activity but depends on a minimal activity threshold for viability. This system provides a platform for defining how SARS-CoV-2 proofreading controls genome stability, viral fitness, and sensitivity to antiviral strategies that exploit reduced replication fidelity. IMPORTANCE Coronaviruses have unusually large RNA genomes because they encode a proofreading enzyme that removes copying errors during replication. It has been unclear whether SARS-CoV-2 can survive when this proofreading function is strongly weakened because earlier studies suggested that loss of the enzyme’s catalytic activity is lethal. We show that SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate substantial impairment of proofreading but only when residual exonuclease activity remains above a minimal threshold. A virus with impaired proofreading replicates less efficiently and accumulates mutations across its genome, whereas a more severe defect prevents virus recovery. These findings clarify how coronavirus proofreading balances genome stability with viral fitness and provide a useful system for studying how reduced replication fidelity affects viral evolution, antiviral sensitivity, and attenuation. Defining this activity threshold may also help guide antiviral strategies that target coronavirus proofreading.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate impaired proofreading activity by its ExoN enzyme, as previous research suggested complete inactivation is lethal, leaving unresolved the virus's capacity for partial proofreading impairment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research employed a continuous fluorescence-based biochemical assay combined with an optimized single-bacmid reverse genetics system to investigate the functional requirement for ExoN in SARS-CoV-2 replication.
analysis.methods: Mutational analysis of residues involved in RNA binding or catalysis was performed, with ExoN activity assessed in vitro, and recombinant SARS-CoV-2 mutants were recovered and evaluated for replication capacity and genome-wide sequence variation via deep sequencing.
analysis.main_results: Mutational analysis revealed graded effects on ExoN activity, with the K9A mutant showing no activity reduction and being readily recovered, the D90A/E92A mutant exhibiting reduced activity and delayed recovery but maintaining substitutions during serial passage, and the K9E mutant being unrecoverable despite repeated attempts; the D90A/E92A mutant displayed a stable mutator phenotype with increased genome-wide sequence variation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate substantial impairment of ExoN activity but depends on a minimal activity threshold for viability, demonstrating a mutator phenotype when proofreading is partially compromised.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This research clarifies how coronavirus proofreading balances genome stability with viral fitness, provides a platform for studying reduced replication fidelity's effects on viral evolution and antiviral sensitivity, and may guide antiviral strategies targeting coronavirus proofreading.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro and may not fully represent in vivo conditions; however, the use of direct biochemical assays and reverse genetics provides high confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 can tolerate impaired proofreading activity by its ExoN enzyme. Using biochemical assays and reverse genetics, the researchers found that partial impairment of ExoN activity is possible but requires a minimal activity threshold for viral viability. Mutants with reduced proofreading (D90A/E92A) exhibited a mutator phenotype with increased genome-wide mutations and reduced replication, while more severe defects (K9E) prevented virus recovery. These findings clarify how coronavirus proofreading balances genome stability and viral fitness, providing insights for antiviral strategies targeting this mechanism.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 冠状病毒 (CoV) 复制异常大的 RNA 基因组,需要由非结构蛋白 14 (nsp14) 和 10 (nsp10) 形成的 3' 至 5' 核糖核酸酶 (ExoN) 进行校对。先前的研究表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 中 ExoN 催化位点的失活是致命的,但该病毒是否能够耐受受损的校对活性仍悬而未决。在这里,我们通过将基于连续荧光的生化测定与优化的单杆粒反向遗传学系统相结合,研究了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 复制中 ExoN 的功能要求。对参与 RNA 结合或催化的残基的突变分析揭示了对 ExoN 体外活性的分级影响。Lys9(位于 RNA 结合界面附近的残基)的丙氨酸取代不会降低 ExoN 活性,而该位置 (K9E) 的电荷反转比催化基序 I 残基 D90 和 E92 (D90A/E92A) 的丙氨酸取代更强烈地损害活性。相应地,携带K9A的重组严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2很容易被恢复,而D90A/E92A突变体仅在较长的延迟后才被恢复,而K9E尽管多次尝试仍无法被拯救。D90A/E92A 突变体表现出复制减少,同时在连续传代期间保持工程化的 ExoN 取代。病毒群体的深度测序揭示了 D90A/E92A 突变体中 基因组 全序列变异的显着增加,证明了稳定的突变体表型。总之,这些发现表明 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 可以耐受 ExoN 活性的严重损害,但取决于生存能力的最小活性阈值。该系统提供了一个平台,用于定义 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 校对如何控制 基因组 稳定性、病毒适应性以及对利用降低的复制保真度的 抗病毒药物 策略的敏感性。重要性冠状病毒具有异常大的 RNA 基因组,因为它们编码一种校对酶,可以消除复制过程中的复制错误。目前还不清楚当这种校对功能被强烈削弱时,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 是否还能生存,因为早期的研究表明,酶催化活性的丧失是致命的。我们表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 可以容忍校对的严重损害,但前提是残余核酸外切酶活性保持在最低阈值以上。校对受损的病毒复制效率较低,并在其 基因组 上累积 突变,而更严重的缺陷会阻止病毒恢复。这些发现阐明了冠状病毒校对如何平衡 基因组 稳定性与病毒适应性,并为研究复制保真度降低如何影响病毒 进化、抗病毒药物 敏感性和衰减提供了有用的系统。定义此活动阈值还可能有助于指导针对冠状病毒校对的 抗病毒药物 策略。

papers.title: Intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine boosting alters immune imprinting and B cell repertoire 2331448
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Immune imprinting is a phenomenon in which prior antigen exposure limits variant-specific de novo immune responses to subsequent related antigens. The serum response to Omicron boosters in mice and human are strongly imprinted by prior vaccines encoding SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-1 spike (e.g., mRNA-1273). Strategies including changes of dosage and interval have had limited success in enhancing variant-specific immunity. Intranasal (i.n.) vaccination is a promising approach that elicits mucosal and systemic immunity. Here we analysed the response of variant boosters delivered i.m. after mRNA-1273 priming at the serum, cellular, and B cell repertoire levels to understand how boosting routes modulate the imprinting effect. Methods C57BL/6 mice were primed i.m. with mRNA-1273 and heterologously boosted i.m. with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine (ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S) against XBB.1.5 spike. Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) were analysed for cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding IgG/IgA. Neutralizing activity was assessed using pseudovirus neutralization assays. Cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding memory B cells (MBCs) in draining lymph nodes (dLNs) were quantified. Ongoing studies are using single-cell BCR sequencing to analyse plasmablast clonotypes, with selected ones expressed as mAbs for functional and epitope analyses. Results Intranasal boosting with ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S against XBB.1.5 spike induced higher fractions of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG and BALF IgA with greater neutralizing activity. Intranasal vaccination increased XBB.1.5-specific MBCs in dLNs, indicating a route-dependent shift in B cell specificity. Conclusion Intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific response at both the serum and cellular levels than i.m. Ongoing B cell repertoire and mAb analyses will provide mechanistic insight into how vaccination route reshapes clonal selection and maturation, informing rational vaccination design. Funding Source Moderna and NIH R01AI157155 Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Immune imprinting limits variant-specific de novo immune responses to subsequent related antigens, and strategies like changing dosage and interval have had limited success in enhancing variant-specific immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: C57BL/6 mice were primed intramuscularly with mRNA-1273 and heterologously boosted intramuscularly with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine against XBB.1.5 spike.
analysis.methods: Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were analysed for cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding IgG/IgA, neutralizing activity was assessed using pseudovirus neutralization assays, and cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding memory B cells in draining lymph nodes were quantified.
analysis.main_results: Intranasal boosting with ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S against XBB.1.5 spike induced higher fractions of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG and BALF IgA with greater neutralizing activity and increased XBB.1.5-specific memory B cells in draining lymph nodes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific response at both the serum and cellular levels than intramuscular boosting, and ongoing B cell repertoire and monoclonal antibody analyses will provide mechanistic insight into how vaccination route reshapes clonal selection and maturation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform rational vaccination design by demonstrating that intranasal boosting can overcome immune imprinting and enhance variant-specific immunity, which is crucial for developing more effective COVID-19 vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted in mice, and ongoing analyses are needed to fully understand the mechanisms; however, the results provide promising insights for vaccine development.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine boosting alters immune imprinting and B cell repertoire. Immune imprinting limits variant-specific responses, and traditional strategies have been ineffective. The researchers primed mice with mRNA-1273 and boosted them intranasally with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine against XBB.1.5 spike. They found that intranasal boosting induced higher levels of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG, BALF IgA, and neutralizing activity, along with increased XBB.1.5-specific memory B cells in draining lymph nodes. This demonstrates that intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific responses than intramuscular boosting. Ongoing analyses of B cell repertoires and monoclonal antibodies will provide further mechanistic insights. These findings are significant for designing more effective vaccines that can overcome immune imprinting.

papers.title_zh: 鼻内 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗 加强改变免疫印记和 B 细胞库 2331448
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Immune imprinting is a phenomenon in which prior antigen exposure limits variant-specific de novo immune responses to subsequent related antigens. The serum response to Omicron boosters in mice and human are strongly imprinted by prior vaccines encoding SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-1 spike (e.g., mRNA-1273). Strategies including changes of dosage and interval have had limited success in enhancing variant-specific immunity. Intranasal (i.n.) vaccination is a promising approach that elicits mucosal and systemic immunity. Here we analysed the response of variant boosters delivered i.m. after mRNA-1273 priming at the serum, cellular, and B cell repertoire levels to understand how boosting routes modulate the imprinting effect. Methods C57BL/6 mice were primed i.m. with mRNA-1273 and heterologously boosted i.m. with a chimpanzee adenoviral-vectored vaccine (ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S) against XBB.1.5 spike. Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) were analysed for cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding IgG/IgA. Neutralizing activity was assessed using pseudovirus neutralization assays. Cross-reactive and strain-specific spike-binding memory B cells (MBCs) in draining lymph nodes (dLNs) were quantified. Ongoing studies are using single-cell BCR sequencing to analyse plasmablast clonotypes, with selected ones expressed as mAbs for functional and epitope analyses. Results Intranasal boosting with ChAd-SARS-CoV-2-S against XBB.1.5 spike induced higher fractions of XBB.1.5-specific serum IgG and BALF IgA with greater neutralizing activity. Intranasal vaccination increased XBB.1.5-specific MBCs in dLNs, indicating a route-dependent shift in B cell specificity. Conclusion Intranasal boosting promotes greater variant-specific response at both the serum and cellular levels than i.m. Ongoing B cell repertoire and mAb analyses will provide mechanistic insight into how vaccination route reshapes clonal selection and maturation, informing rational vaccination design. Funding Source Moderna and NIH R01AI157155 Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 免疫印记是一种现象,其中先前的抗原暴露将变异特异性从头 免疫应答 限制到随后的相关抗原。小鼠和人类对 Omicron 加强剂的血清反应受到先前编码 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Wuhan-1 刺突(例如 mRNA-1273)的 疫苗 的强烈影响。包括改变剂量和间隔时间在内的策略在增强变异特异性免疫方面取得的成功有限。鼻内 (i.n.) 疫苗接种 是一种有前景的方法,可引发粘膜和全身免疫。在这里,我们分析了即时交付的变体增强剂的反应。在血清、细胞和 B 细胞库水平上启动 mRNA-1273 后,了解增强途径如何调节印记效应。方法 C57BL/6 小鼠经肌肉注射初免。与 mRNA-1273 和异源加强肌肉注射。使用黑猩猩腺病毒载体 疫苗 (ChAd-严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2-S) 对抗 XBB.1.5 刺突。分析血清和支气管肺泡灌洗液 (BALF) 的交叉反应性和菌株特异性尖峰结合 IgG/IgA。使用假病毒中和测定来评估中和活性。对引流淋巴结 (dLN) 中的交叉反应和菌株特异性尖峰结合记忆 B 细胞 (MBC) 进行了定量。正在进行的研究正在使用单细胞 BCR 测序来分析浆母细胞克隆型,并选择表达为 mAb 的克隆型进行功能和表位分析。结果 针对 XBB.1.5 尖峰的 ChAd-严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2-S 鼻内加强诱导了更高比例的 XBB.1.5 特异性血清 IgG 和 BALF IgA,具有更高的中和活性。鼻内 疫苗接种 增加了 dLN 中的 XBB.1.5 特异性 MBC,表明 B 细胞特异性存在途径依赖性转变。结论 与肌内注射相比,鼻内加强在血清和细胞水平上促进更大的变异特异性反应。正在进行的 B 细胞库和 mAb 分析将为 疫苗接种 途径如何重塑克隆选择和成熟提供机制见解,为合理的 疫苗接种 设计提供信息。资金来源 Moderna 和 NIH R01AI157155 主题类别 疫苗 和免疫疗法 (VAC)

papers.title: Prevalence and Determinants of Hospital-Acquired Infections in Intensive Care Units Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Descriptive Surveillance Study at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Iran.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Hospital‐acquired infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) cause significant morbidity, mortality, and costs. The COVID‐19 pandemic intensified infection control, but its effect on HAI prevalence and patterns is unclear. This study compared HAI prevalence, types, and causative agents in an Iranian tertiary hospital before and after COVID‐19. Methods A retrospective descriptive‐analytical study was conducted on ICU patients admitted to Taleghani Hospital, Kermanshah, Iran, between 2019 and 2020. Demographic, clinical, and microbiological data were collected from hospital records. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using Chi‐square or Fisher's exact tests, and continuous non‐normally distributed variables were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results Among 1778 ICU admissions, 301 cases of HAIs were identified, yielding an overall prevalence of 16.9%. The prevalence decreased from 131/718 (18.2%) in 2019 to 170/1060 (16.0%) in 2020. Gram‐negative aerobic bacteria were the predominant pathogens in both years (128/131 [97.7%] vs. 163/170 [95.9%]), while fungal and other infections emerged only in 2020. Ventilator‐associated events (VAE) were the most frequent infection type, followed by pneumonia, urinary tract infections (UTIs), surgical site infections (SSIs), and bloodstream infections (BSIs). While VAE and pneumonia decreased in 2020, UTIs and BSIs increased. ICU2 consistently reported the highest infection rates, whereas ICU3 experienced a marked rise in infections in 2020. Statistical analysis confirmed significant associations between infection occurrence and gender, ICU ward, and Gram‐negative bacterial infections (p < 0.05). Conclusion Despite strengthened infection control during COVID‐19, HAIs particularly Gram‐negative infections and VAE remain prevalent in ICUs. Continuous surveillance and targeted interventions are essential to reduce their burden.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and determinants of hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) in an Iranian tertiary hospital before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aimed to understand how the pandemic affected HAI patterns, as HAIs are a significant cause of morbidity, mortality, and costs. A retrospective descriptive-analytical study was conducted on ICU patients admitted between 2019 and 2020, collecting demographic, clinical, and microbiological data. Statistical analyses were used to assess associations between infection occurrence and factors such as gender, ICU ward, and Gram-negative bacterial infections. The authors concluded that HAIs, particularly Gram-negative infections and ventilator-associated events (VAE), remain prevalent in ICUs despite pandemic-related infection control measures. papers.title_zh: Prevalence and Determinants of Hospital-Acquired Infections in Intensive Care Units Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Descriptive Surveillance Study at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Iran.
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Hospital‐acquired infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) cause significant morbidity, mortality, and costs. The COVID‐19 pandemic intensified infection control, but its effect on HAI prevalence and patterns is unclear. This study compared HAI prevalence, types, and causative agents in an Iranian tertiary hospital before and after COVID‐19. Methods A retrospective descriptive‐analytical study was conducted on ICU patients admitted to Taleghani Hospital, Kermanshah, Iran, between 2019 and 2020. Demographic, clinical, and microbiological data were collected from hospital records. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using Chi‐square or Fisher's exact tests, and continuous non‐normally distributed variables were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results Among 1778 ICU admissions, 301 cases of HAIs were identified, yielding an overall prevalence of 16.9%. The prevalence decreased from 131/718 (18.2%) in 2019 to 170/1060 (16.0%) in 2020. Gram‐negative aerobic bacteria were the predominant pathogens in both years (128/131 [97.7%] vs. 163/170 [95.9%]), while fungal and other infections emerged only in 2020. Ventilator‐associated events (VAE) were the most frequent infection type, followed by pneumonia, urinary tract infections (UTIs), surgical site infections (SSIs), and bloodstream infections (BSIs). While VAE and pneumonia decreased in 2020, UTIs and BSIs increased. ICU2 consistently reported the highest infection rates, whereas ICU3 experienced a marked rise in infections in 2020. Statistical analysis confirmed significant associations between infection occurrence and gender, ICU ward, and Gram‐negative bacterial infections (p < 0.05). Conclusion Despite strengthened infection control during COVID‐19, HAIs particularly Gram‐negative infections and VAE remain prevalent in ICUs. Continuous surveillance and targeted interventions are essential to reduce their burden.

papers.title: Persistent SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein in Vasculitic Skin Lesions after Infection or mRNA Vaccination: A Retrospective Case control Immunofluorescence Study.
papers.abstract: Vasculitic skin lesions have been reported in association with both SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination. Whether viral proteins persist in lesional vessels beyond the acute phase remains unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the presence of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in persistent or delayed-onset cutaneous vasculitis temporally associated with COVID-19 infection or vaccination. This retrospective case-control study includes 9 patients with persistent or delayed-onset vasculitic skin lesions following COVID-19 infection (n=4) or mRNA vaccination (n=5). Skin biopsies were analysed using immunofluorescence for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Prepandemic leukocytoclastic vasculitis (n=3) and healthy postinfection/postvaccination skin (n=3) served as controls. Spike protein was detected in vascular endothelial cells of all 9 patients with COVID-19- or vaccine-associated vasculitis. Staining was absent in all prepandemic vasculitis and healthy control samples. Histopathology showed typical features of leukocytoclastic vasculitis without evidence of viral cytopathic changes. We found that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein can persist in endothelial cells of vasculitic skin lesions weeks to months after COVID-19 infection or mRNA vaccination. These findings suggest that retained viral proteins may contribute to prolonged or delayed-onset vasculitic skin manifestations. Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying spike persistence and its clinical significance.

papers.title: Seroprevalence and risk factors for SARS-CoV-2 infection among unvaccinated adults in a rural community in South-East Nigeria during the Omicron era: a community-based cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection is an emerging viral disease that became a global pandemic in March 2020. Despite the protracted pandemic, population-based local data on the burden and exposure risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection remain limited in most parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where the pandemic surprisingly defied early public health predictions. A community-based cross-sectional study of 252 consenting unvaccinated adults was conducted from March 11 to June 12, 2022, in Enugu State, southeastern Nigeria. A two-stage cluster sampling design was used, with a validated, interviewer-administered questionnaire adapted from the World Health Organization Unity Study Protocol, to collect demographic, socio-behavioural, and clinical data. Each participant was tested for SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariate analysis was used to determine factors independently associated with SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity. A P-value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The mean age was 47.72 ± 17.92 years, with 57.14% (144) female. The seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 (IgG or IgM) was 67.90%. Thirty-nine (15.48%) out of 252 participants had both SARS-CoV-2 IgG and IgM antibodies. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that healthcare workers had significantly higher odds of SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity than non-healthcare workers (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.83, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.52–9.66; P = 0.004). Serological evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection was observed in approximately two out of every three unvaccinated adults, indicating widespread previous exposure through natural infection in the study population by the first half of 2022. The predominance of SARS-CoV-2 IgG over IgM antibodies suggests that most infections occurred before sample collection and is consistent with declining community transmission during the study period. Healthcare worker status was independently associated with SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity, reinforcing the importance of strengthening infection prevention and control measures to protect frontline healthcare workers during future emerging infectious disease outbreaks.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年 3 月 11 日至 6 月 12 日,在尼日利亚东南部埃努古州对 252 名同意的未接种疫苗的成年人进行了一项基于社区的横断面研究。252 名参与者中有 39 名 (15.48%) 同时具有 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG 和 IgM 抗体。

elements_zh.main_results: The seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 (IgG or IgM) was 67.90%. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG 相对于 IgM 抗体的优势表明大多数感染发生在样本采集之前,并且与研究期间 传播 社区的下降相一致。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在大约三分之二的未接种疫苗的成年人中观察到 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的血清学证据,表明到 2022 年上半年,研究人群中通过自然感染广泛存在先前的暴露。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: P 值 < 0.05 被认为具有统计显着性。该研究是在一个农村社区进行的,这可能会限制普遍性。

papers.title: Identifying the Most Important Influencing Factors Based on Demographic Information, Nutrition, Physical Activity, Leisure Time, and Underlying Diseases in the Severity of Disease in COVID-19 Patients Using Data Mining Techniques.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims The COVID‐19 pandemic has affected millions of individuals worldwide and resulted in substantial mortality. Data mining and machine learning techniques enable the analysis of comprehensive patient data, facilitating the identification of key patterns and determinants that support clinical and preventive decision‐making. Methods This study evaluates the performance of three machine learning approaches—Deep Learning, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—in identifying factors associated with COVID‐19 severity. A comparative analysis based on ROC curves and quantitative performance metrics demonstrates that Deep Learning and GBDT outperform SVM. Results All models consistently identify hypertension as a major risk factor. However, differences emerge in other influential variables: GBDT ranks hypertension as the most significant factor, followed by stomach ulcers, whereas Deep Learning highlights vitamin intake as the primary determinant. The deep learning tree variant further supports the importance of vitamin consumption. Conclusion The superior predictive performance of Deep Learning and GBDT provides a reliable benchmark and yields novel insights, including the potential roles of stomach ulcers and vitamin intake in disease severity. These findings emphasize the value of employing multiple high‐performing models and robust validation strategies for accurate identification of clinical risk factors in COVID‐19.
